verdict.rationale: Cline documents its own programmatic surfaces: an SDK described as built on 'the same core engine' behind the CLI, Kanban, VS Code and JetBrains, a headless CLI for scripts and automation, and ACP so any compatible client can drive the same agent. Nothing documents that every UI action (diff review, checkpoints and undo, Kanban card management) is reachable programmatically, and no machine-readable API spec is published; the hosted gateway only exposes an OpenAI-format Chat Completions endpoint. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, documented programmatic equivalents for UI-only features like diff review, checkpoints and Kanban management, a published OpenAPI or SDK reference, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Build AI agents and integrations powered by the same core engine behind the CLI, Kanban, VS Code extension, and JetBrains plugin.
Use headless mode for scripts/automation and processable output.
Any ACP-capable client can use Cline as its coding agent without a dedicated extension — the same agent you use in the terminal, embedded in the tool you're already working in.
cline --auto-approve true "run tests and fix failures"
